as_told.title: Former NASA engineer on electromagnetic anomalies near Bermuda Triangle

plain: The Bermuda Triangle, a stretch of the Atlantic Ocean long known for stories of lost ships and planes, is said to show real, measurable oddities. A retired US Navy admiral named Tim Gallaudet says on the show that there seems to be "data" and "evidence of anomalies" there. He speaks as a former senior official, though he does not say what the data is. Michels tells a similar version that he heard from a former NASA engineer, NASA being the US space agency. In that version, there is "a little patch" in or near the Triangle with "tons of electromagnetic anomalies", meaning strange readings in magnetic and electrical fields. So one teller speaks of official data in general, and the other of electromagnetic readings passed on secondhand. If true, it would mean something physical and unexplained is going on in that patch of ocean.
